blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Customer e-mail address written to the error log on a failed lookup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail when only the name is needed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (e.g. `throw new NotFoundError("no customer for this e-mail")`). When an agent looks up an address that matches no customer, `errorHandler` (src/server.ts:14, `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`) writes the typed e-mail address to the application log, which then holds personal data with no purpose or retention rule — GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation and 5(1)(e) storage limitation; the criterion "No personal data goes to logs" fails.
findings.title: Customer e-mail address written to the error log on a failed lookup

findings.evidence:
id: String(customer.id),
name: customer.name,
email: customer.email,
phone: customer.phone,
birthDate: customer.birth_date,
address: customer.address,
findings.recommendation: The proposal's purpose is that the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to": send only `id` and `name` to Helply, and drop `email`, `phone`, `birthDate` and `address` (and select only `id, name` in `customerById`, src/support.ts:28). Every signed-in customer who opens the chat currently has their phone number, date of birth and postal address shipped to the third-party chat vendor through `GET /chat/settings` — GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 25 data protection by default.
findings.title: Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail when only the name is needed

findings.recommendation: Question for the team: is Helply already a processor under contract (GDPR Art. 28), listed in the records of processing (Art. 30), and where does it process the data — inside the EEA, or under a Chapter V transfer mechanism? The proposal names "the chat vendor" but neither the processor nor the transfer.
findings.title: Helply is a new processor with no stated agreement or transfer location

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The stated purpose is that agents stop asking customers "to repeat who they are"; `POST /support/customers/lookup` returns the whole record, birth date and postal address included, to every support agent. Return only the fields agents need to identify the customer (id, name, e-mail), or state in the plan why the others are needed — GDPR Art. 5(1)(c). Confidence low: what agents need was not visible in the plan.
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date, phone and address beyond identifying the customer
